pageCache.text:
Welcome to our school
We are a one form entry Catholic primary school and in our school the children are at the very centre of everything we do. We are committed to ensuring we deliver the highest quality education through exploration, enjoyment and creativity. We work hard to ensure our children fulfil and achieve their full potential and be the best they can be.
Everyone is welcome at our school. We are a rich, diverse and vibrant community. All the children are known as individuals, and their talents and strengths recognised. As a school we will ensure your child is safe, happy and making progress. We believe children should feel welcome, inspired and supported when they are learning. We celebrate the individuality of all children.
Mrs Claire O'Rourke Headteacher

Breakfast and After School Club
Registration – Required for All Children
Before booking any sessions, parents must complete a registration form for each child. This provides us with essential information such as emergency contacts and medical needs. A copy of the form is attached; if you would prefer a paper copy sent home with your child, please contact the school office.
If you are likely to use the clubs occasionally, we still advise completing a form in advance to avoid last‑minute delays.

Times and availability
Breakfast Club will run Monday to Friday, 7.45am – 8.45am (term time only).
The cost is £5 per session.
After School Club will run Monday to Friday, 3.20pm – 5.30pm (term time only).
The cost is £8 per session.

Children can enjoy a range of activities including colouring, games, Lego, reading and outdoor play (weather permitting).

Spaces and Availability
At the moment both breakfast and after school club will have a maximum amount of 15 spaces available. Both clubs are available to all children from Reception to Year 6.
Bookings and payments will be made via Arbor.
Payments can be made by topping up your Arbor account in advance, allowing for a convenient and secure way to manage your child's club fees. Enrichment Clubs
At St Mary Star of the Sea School, we run a number of Enrichment clubs after school on Mondays to Thursdays. These clubs are run by school and also by external organisations, such as Funk Fusion, Zylo and Upgrade Martial Arts.
Please see the Timetable of clubs below:
Registration and payment for school run enrichment clubs are made via Arbor and are on a 2-term basis. Booking is on a first come first served basis. Your child's place in a club is not secure until full payment has been made.
External Clubs
External clubs will have their own registration process, which may not follow the school run club two-termly schedule.
Please contact these companies directly for more information (provided below). Bookings for some of the external clubs will be made available starting in September and are on a first come first served basis (The providers will communicate this when they are ready).

Prospective Parents
Information for Prospective Parents
Thank-you for taking the time to visit our website. We have prepared a number of resources to give you a feel and an insight to what our school can offer your child and family.
If your child was born between 01.09.2022 and 31.08.2023, it is now time to apply for a school place. Parents and carers are requested to apply online via East Sussex County Council website at www.eastsussex.gov.uk/schools . The online application system closes on January 15th 2027. Please see the East Sussex website for further information.
Please below to download our current prospectus.

NOTE: Parents with a child/children already on roll at the school are still required to apply for a place for their younger child and submit supporting evidence, as specified above, as places are not allocated to siblings automatically.

If you require any further information please contact Miss Louise Basson, the School Admissions Officer via the school office.

Governors
Local Governing Committee (LGC)
Hello and Welcome to St Mary Star of the Sea's Local Governing Committee (LGC) Section.
The main functions of a Governing Committee are to ensure clarity of the school’s vision and purpose, to hold the Headteacher and staff to account and to oversee the school’s financial performance. In our case, we also ensure that the school retains its distinctiveness as a Catholic school, based on Gospel values.
Our Constitution specifies that there shall be six Governors, representing our Diocese/Bishop (Foundation Governors) and the parent body. The role of a Governor is voluntary, but it is a privilege to work as a team to serve the best interests of our school.

pageCache.pageTitle: St Mary Star of the Sea Catholic Primary School - Welcome
pageCache.text:
Welcome
Live, love and learn in God's name
Headteacher's Welcome
Thank you for taking the time to visit our school page. We are a Catholic primary school where children are at the very heart of everything we do. We are committed to delivering the highest quality education through exploration, enjoyment and creativity, and we work hard to ensure every child fulfils their potential and becomes the very best they can be.
Everyone is welcome at our school. We are a rich, diverse and vibrant community where every child is known as an individual and their talents and strengths are recognised. We are dedicated to ensuring that your child feels safe, happy and is making strong progress. We believe that children learn best when they feel welcomed, inspired and supported, and we celebrate the uniqueness of every child.
Our Catholic values underpin all that we do and give our school its distinctive character. We value the strong links between school, home and parish, recognising the shared responsibility we all have in nurturing our children. As a Catholic community, we celebrate our children’s successes in all aspects of school life, showing them that we believe in them, respect them and are proud of them.
We are proud to be a Catholic Academy within the Bosco Catholic Education Trust, and we warmly welcome families of all faiths and beliefs, as well as those with none.
Please explore our website to see all that our school has to offer.

SEND
At St Mary Star of the Sea School we aim to provide opportunities for all our children to be able to reach their aspirations, irrespective of their starting point or educational needs. We strive to enable our children to become resilient, well-rounded lifelong learners.
As a school we are mindful of and comply with the Government’s Special Educational Needs and Disability Code of Practice. Every teacher is a teacher of every child, including those with special educational needs and disabilities. We respect the unique contribution, which every individual can make to our school community.
The achievement, attitude and well-being of every child at St Mary Star of the Sea matters and inclusion is the responsibility of everyone within our school.

Sports Premium
PE
Physical Education (PE) at SMSS
Let us run with perseverance the race marked out for us.
St Mary star of the Sea Catholic Primary School believes that Physical Education (PE), experienced in a safe and supportive environment, is essential to ensure children attain optimum physical and emotional development and good health. We intend to deliver high-quality teaching and learning opportunities that inspire all children to succeed in physical education and in developing life skills. We want to teach children skills to keep them safe such as being able to swim (y3). We also want to teach children how to cooperate and collaborate with others as part of an effective team, understanding fairness and equity of play to embed life-long values. Our curriculum aims to improve the wellbeing and fitness of all children at SMSS, not only through the sporting skills taught, but through the underpinning values and disciplines PE promotes. Through our enrichment program we also offer Wild Beach and Forest School sessions. These give the opportunity to explore, experience and enjoy the environment and natural world with a tailored Forest and Wild Beach programme delivered by trained staff.

St Mary Star of the Sea receives PE and sport funding from the Departments for Education, Health and Culture, Media and Sport. We recognise that we have a central role to play in providing children with a varied PE curriculum, extra curriculuar activities and enrichment experiences which will support our children's health, growth and development.

English
English at SMSS
At St Mary Star of the Sea, we aim to provide pupils with a high quality education in English. Our writing curriculum is rooted in reading, with all writing opportunities linked to a high quality class text. We ensure the text provides an opportunity for the pupils to delve deeper into the project they are learning about. See the links below for how this is planned out.
Progression in Writing
Reading @ SMSS
At St. Mary Star of the Sea we recognise the importance of reading in all areas of the the curriculum. Therefore we strive to put reading at the heart of all we do in order to create children that 'Learn to read then read to learn'. To help us do this we use an online platform called 'Accelerated Reader'.
'Accelerated Reader' is a powerful tool for monitoring and managing independent reading practice while promoting reading for pleasure. At it's heart, Accelerated Reader is simple. A child reads a book, takes an online quiz and gets immediate feedback. Children respond to regular feedback and are motivated to make progress with their reading skills.

Our school library has been designed to be a place where children can come and let their imagination take them anywhere. We have a lunchtime library club and the chidlren are able to take books home. Reading is at the heart of all we do...
Library Drop in Sessions... See Below For Details
Accelerated reader is used in Keystage Two and for those children who are ready to move on from bookbands. Your child will be provided with their own username and a password and can then access this from home by following this link: http://ukhosted130.renlearn.co.uk/6709796/
Writing @ SMSS
At St. Mary Star of the Sea, we understand that writing is an essential part of the curriculum; we’re ambitious about what all children can achieve, and we strive to create exciting and stimulating writing opportunities for all children. We aim to ensure that all children leave our school with a passion for writing and a high level of English knowledge and skills that they can apply in a variety of subjects and situations. In order for children to be able to do this, we immerse them in a rich-text environment that provides models and examples of high-quality writing which children can examine and explore. We use a text-based approach that is carefully planned and structured.
We follow the Read Write Inc Spelling programme. This is a 15minute a day programme which goes from Year 2 - Year 6. Read Write Inc is a spelling programme based on proven strategies of teacher modelling followed by partner work, to embed learning.
